description: Mistake Pattern AI - Deep analysis engine that identifies specific patterns in wrong answers beyond simple topic-level accuracy. Detects patterns like 'misses LIFO/FIFO questions when framed as ratio impacts', 'calculation errors under time pressure', 'confuses similar concepts'. Generates actionable insights per pattern.
steps: Create src/features/mistake-patterns/ directory with types/, utils/, components/, and __tests__/ subdirectories

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/types/index.ts with interfaces: MistakePattern (id, patternType: 'conceptConfusion' | 'framingTrap' | 'calculationError' | 'timePressure' | 'misreadQuestion', description, affectedTopics, occurrenceCount, examples: QuestionExample[], severity: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low', recommendation), PatternAnalysis (patterns, overallInsight, studyPlan), QuestionExample (questionId, questionText, selectedAnswer, correctAnswer, topic)

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/utils/pattern-detector.ts implementing: (1) detectConceptConfusion() - finds pairs of related topics where student gets one right and the other wrong consistently, (2) detectFramingTraps() - identifies when same concept is missed only under certain question phrasing, (3) detectTimePressureErrors() - correlates wrong answers with short time spent (< 30s per question), (4) detectCalculationErrors() - finds wrong answers where correct answer was adjacent option (indicating math mistakes), (5) detectConfidenceCalibration() - finds patterns where high confidence + wrong answer (misconceptions)

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/utils/pattern-storage.ts to cache pattern analysis results in localStorage with a 'last analyzed' timestamp, re-analyzing only when new attempts are added (key: 'cfa-buddy-mistake-patterns')

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/utils/insight-generator.ts that takes detected patterns and generates human-readable insight strings: specific, actionable statements like 'You miss 73% of LIFO/FIFO questions when they ask about ratio impacts rather than direct inventory values'

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/components/pattern-dashboard.tsx - client component displaying: (1) top patterns sorted by severity, (2) each pattern with its description, affected topics, occurrence frequency, and specific question examples, (3) overall insight summary, (4) 'drill this pattern' CTA buttons
Create src/features/mistake-patterns/components/pattern-card.tsx - reusable card component for displaying a single mistake pattern with an icon, severity badge, description, and example

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/__tests__/pattern-detector.test.ts testing: (1) detects concept confusion when student misses related topics, (2) detects time pressure when fast wrong answers, (3) detects calculation errors from adjacent-answer selections, (4) returns empty patterns for new users, (5) correctly counts pattern occurrences, (6) assigns appropriate severity levels

Create src/features/mistake-patterns/__tests__/insight-generator.test.ts testing: (1) generates specific human-readable insights, (2) includes actual numbers (percentages, counts), (3) handles edge cases (single occurrence patterns, no patterns)
Add route page at src/app/(protected)/mistakes/patterns/page.tsx rendering the pattern dashboard
Link from the existing Mistakes page to the pattern analysis page
acceptance_criteria: Running npm run test passes all new tests
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors
Pattern detector identifies at least 5 distinct pattern types from practice attempt data
Insights are specific and actionable (include percentages, topic names, specific observations)
Pattern dashboard renders with severity-sorted patterns and examples
verification: eval "$(mise activate bash)" && npm run test
eval "$(mise activate bash)" && npm run build
findings: All 560 tests passing (25 new). Build succeeds. TypeScript clean. Pattern detector handles edge case where slowErrorRate is 0 by treating any fast errors as significant (Infinity ratio). The PatternType union uses 'confidenceMismatch' instead of 'misreadQuestion' from the plan - this better matches the actual algorithm implemented.
